fixtures.basis: Alabama's State Building Code covers only state-owned or state-funded buildings, K-12 schools, public colleges, hotels, motels and movie theaters, so Mobile's own plumbing and building codes set the counts for private offices and restaurants. Mobile leaves Table 403.1 of the 2021 International Plumbing Code, the half-and-half split, the rounding rule, the urinal substitution rule (424.2) and the small-occupancy exceptions (403.2 exceptions 2 to 4) unamended: its Chapter 4 amendments were read in full on the city's PDF. It deletes two exceptions about all-gender multi-user rooms. The unamended table rows and sections were read on UpCodes' copy of the 2021 code as adopted in Alabama (secondary; UpCodes has no Mobile edition).

amendment.text: Mobile deletes (1) the exception that lets the fixture count for a multi-user room serving all genders be worked on 100% of the occupants (IPC 403.1.1 exception 2 and IBC 2902.1.1 exception 2) and (2) the exception that lets a room designed for use by both sexes take the place of separate facilities (IPC 403.2 exception 6). The toilet ratios, the split, rounding and urinal substitution are unchanged, so the worked examples equal the state pack's.
amendment.quote: 403.1.1 Fixture calculations. Delete Exception #2 in its entirety. [...] 403.2 Separate Facilities. Delete Exception #6 in its entirety [Plumbing Code ordinance, Article Eleven] | 2902.1.1 Fixture Calculations. Delete Exception 2 [Building Code ordinance, Article Thirteen]
amendment.deleted_text_quote: [403.1.1 exception 2] Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load. In such multiple-user facilities, each fixture type shall be in accordance with ICC A117.1 and each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall. [403.2 exception 6] Separate facilities shall not be required where rooms having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by both sexes and privacy for water closets is provided in accordance with Section 405.3.4. Urinals shall be located in an area visually separated from the remainder of the facility or each urinal that is provided shall be located in a stall.
amendment.note: The Building Code ordinance deletes only 2902.1.1 exception 2; it does not delete the matching exception 6 of IBC 2902.2, so the building code and plumbing code texts differ on shared all-gender rooms.

office.quote: Business: Buildings for the transaction of business, professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, ambulatory care, light industrial and similar uses: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50

restaurant.quote: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts d | 1 per 75 | 1 per 75

table_rows.split_rounding_quote: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. [...] Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number.
table_rows.urinal_quote: In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies.
table_rows.separate_rooms_quote: Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer.
table_rows.stall_quote: Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy. [...] Each urinal utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate area with walls or partitions to provide privacy.

worked_examples.how: 25 women, 25 men. 1 per 25 for the first 50: 25/25 = 1 each. Urinals may replace up to 50% of 1 = 0.5, so none.
50 women, 50 men. 50/25 = 2 each. Urinals may replace up to 50% of 2 = 1.
100 women, 100 men. First 50: 2; remaining 50 at 1 per 50: 1; total 3 each. Urinals up to 50% of 3 = 1.5, so 1.
200 women, 200 men. First 50: 2; remaining 150 at 1 per 50: 3; total 5 each. Urinals up to 50% of 5 = 2.5, so 2.
25 each. 25/75 = 0.33, rounds up to 1 each. Urinals up to 67% of 1 = 0.67, so none.
50 each. 50/75 = 0.67, rounds up to 1 each. Urinals up to 67% of 1 = 0.67, so none.
100 each. 100/75 = 1.33, rounds up to 2 each. Urinals up to 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 each. 200/75 = 2.67, rounds up to 3 each. Urinals up to 67% of 3 = 2.01, so 2.
25 each. 25/50 = 0.5, rounds up to 1 each. Urinals up to 67% of 1 = 0.67, so none.
50 each. 50/50 = 1 each. Urinals up to 67% of 1 = 0.67, so none.
100 each. 100/50 = 2 each. Urinals up to 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 each. 200/50 = 4 each. Urinals up to 67% of 4 = 2.68, so 2.

fixtures.worked_examples_note: Same figures as the Alabama state pack: Mobile changes no ratio. The urinal limit applies 'in each bathroom or toilet room'; the figures assume one men's room holds all the men's fixtures. Urinals are optional, never required. Mobile adds that restrooms with urinals, other than residential, need a floor drain (IPC 413.5 as amended).

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Mobile job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material for Gulf Coast humidity and see the rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Mobile offices, schools, restaurants and port warehouses, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Mobile's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Mobile sets the number of toilets by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
extra_rule_bullets: - **Mobile access rules:** Mobile's plan form for commercial projects asks whether the design meets the access chapter of the city's building rules and a national accessibility standard in its 2017 edition. The federal rules apply as well.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** under Mobile's plumbing rules a one-person restroom is marked as open to everyone. Mobile took out of its plumbing rules the provision that lets a shared all-gender room take the place of separate men's and women's rooms, so ask Build Mobile before you plan one. Alabama law requires shared restrooms in public K-12 schools and public colleges to be designated for one sex.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Mobile requires a permit to alter a building unless the work is on its exempt list. The list covers "painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work" and movable partitions up to 5 feet 9 inches high. It doesn't name toilet partitions, which are fixed in place. Ask Build Mobile, the city's permitting department, whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.stalls_intro: Alabama has no statewide building rules for private commercial buildings, so Mobile's own rules decide. Mobile counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and fractions round up. Every toilet needs a stall. Urinals are optional: in a men's room they may replace up to two thirds of the toilets in a restaurant or school and up to half in an office, and each urinal needs a privacy screen.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building, and at least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. An office designed for 25 people or fewer, a shop designed for 100 or fewer, and any building designed for 15 or fewer, doesn't need separate men's and women's rooms. Schools, hotels and movie theaters also come under Alabama's state building rules, which use the same counts. Confirm the count with Build Mobile.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, Mobile's building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20. Mobile's plan form for commercial projects asks for the figure.
page.install_rule: Mobile requires a contractor on building work that needs a permit to be licensed and bonded under city and state requirements, to register with the building official and to keep a $10,000 bond on file with the city. Alabama requires a state general contractor license for commercial jobs of $100,000 or more. Confirm what your project needs with Build Mobile. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: A contractor on permitted building work in Mobile must be licensed, bonded and registered with the city.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** Alabama has no state wage law for public jobs, so a set wage applies only on federally funded work. For a carpenter on building work in Mobile County the federal rate is $18.16 an hour, with no benefits amount set.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 10% in Mobile: 4% state, 1% Mobile County and 5% city.
page.buyers_extra: - **Shipyards, port terminals and aircraft plants:** HDPE or phenolic in shop-floor restrooms open to the humid Gulf air, with hardware that takes hard use.
sources: - Codes Mobile enforces: City of Mobile, [An Ordinance to Adopt a Building Code for the City of Mobile](https://www.buildmobile.org/uploads/2021IBCLocalAmendmentEffectiveJanuary72023.pdf) (2021 International Building Code with Mobile amendments) and [An Ordinance to Adopt a Plumbing Code for the City of Mobile](https://www.buildmobile.org/uploads/2021IPCLocalAmendmentEffectiveJanuary72023.pdf) (2021 International Plumbing Code with Mobile amendments), both adopted November 8, 2022 and listed on Build Mobile's [Forms, Applications and Codes](https://www.buildmobile.org/forms-and-applications/) page; effective date in the city notice [Adopted fire, construction trade and maintenance codes](https://www.cityofmobile.gov/news/adopted-fire-construction-trade-and-maintenance-codes) (January 7, 2023); codes in use today on the [Building Code Summary for all commercial projects, revised November 2026](https://www.buildmobile.org/uploads/BuildingCodeSummary-pn-COMRev7.pdf). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Toilet counts in Mobile: Plumbing Code of the City of Mobile, [ordinance amendments to Chapter 4](https://www.buildmobile.org/uploads/2021IPCLocalAmendmentEffectiveJanuary72023.pdf) (Sections 403.1.1 and 403.2) and [Building Code ordinance](https://www.buildmobile.org/uploads/2021IBCLocalAmendmentEffectiveJanuary72023.pdf), Section 2902.1.1. The unamended Table 403.1 and Sections 403.1.1, 403.1.2, 403.2, 405.3.4, 405.3.5 and 424.2 of the 2021 International Plumbing Code were read on a [secondary copy of the code as adopted in Alabama](https://up.codes/viewer/alabama/ipc-2021/chapter/4/fixtures-faucets-and-fixture-fittings). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Floor area per person and the fire test for solid plastic: 2021 International Building Code as adopted by Mobile, Table 1004.5, Sections 803.9 and 803.1.1 (NFPA 286) and the definition of interior wall and ceiling finish, not amended by the city, read on a secondary copy of the code as adopted in Alabama ([Chapter 10](https://up.codes/viewer/alabama/ibc-2021/chapter/10/means-of-egress), [Chapter 8](https://up.codes/viewer/alabama/ibc-2021/chapter/8/interior-finishes), [Chapter 2](https://up.codes/viewer/alabama/ibc-2021/chapter/2/definitions)). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Permits and work exempt from a permit in Mobile: [Building Code ordinance](https://www.buildmobile.org/uploads/2021IBCLocalAmendmentEffectiveJanuary72023.pdf), Section 105, and [Existing Building Code ordinance](https://www.buildmobile.org/uploads/2021IEBCLocalAmendmentEffectiveJanuary72023.pdf), Section 105; the unamended lists in Section 105.2 of the 2021 International Building Code and 2021 International Existing Building Code were read on secondary copies ([building code, Chapter 1](https://up.codes/viewer/alabama/ibc-2021/chapter/1/scope-and-administration), [existing building code, Chapter 1](https://up.codes/viewer/alabama/iebc-2021/chapter/1/scope-and-administration)); department contacts on [Build Mobile, Contact](https://www.buildmobile.org/contact/). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Restrooms in public schools and colleges: Code of Alabama Section 16-1-54 and [Senate Bill 129 of 2024, enrolled (Act 2024-34)](https://alison.legislature.state.al.us/files/pdf/SearchableInstruments/2024RS/SB129-enr.pdf). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Mobile contractor rules: [Building Code ordinance](https://www.buildmobile.org/uploads/2021IBCLocalAmendmentEffectiveJanuary72023.pdf), Articles Four and Five (license, registration and $10,000 bond). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Sales tax in Mobile: Alabama Department of Revenue, [current local tax rates file](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/taxrates_current.csv) (City of Mobile general sales tax 5% since November 1, 2012; Mobile County 1% inside the corporate limits of Mobile and Prichard), [City and County Tax Rates](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/sales-use/city-and-county-tax-rates/) and [State Sales and Use Tax Rates](https://www.revenue.alabama.gov/sales-use/state-sales-use-tax-rates/) (4%). Checked 2026-11-24.

- Mobile County carpenter rate on federally funded building work: [federal wage determination AL20260092, modification 1, May 18, 2026](https://sam.gov/wage-determination/AL20260092/1). Checked 2026-11-24.

notes: To confirm by phone before launch: whether replacing or adding toilet partitions in an existing commercial restroom needs a Mobile permit (Build Mobile, Permitting, 251-208-7602, permitting@cityofmobile.org).

Mobile's plumbing code ordinance deletes the shared all-gender room exception, but its building code ordinance leaves the matching exception in place: ask Build Mobile (Inspections, 251-208-7198) how it treats a shared all-gender room.

The unamended parts of Mobile's codes (toilet table, exempt-work list, floor area per person, the HDPE fire-test section, single-user restroom signs) were read on UpCodes' Alabama copies of the 2021 codes, not on ICC's site: check once in a browser at codes.iccsafe.org.
The fire-test section says 'used as an interior finish'; the code's definition of interior finish names toilet room privacy partitions.
Effective date: the city's notice and the ordinance file names say January 7, 2023; the city's Build Mobile department page says February 7, 2023.
The building code ordinance still says work over $50,000 needs a general contractor under state law; the state threshold has been $100,000 since October 1, 2024, and the page uses the state figure.
Job sites in Mobile County outside the city limits follow the county's codes (2024 editions since July 1, 2026) and a 1.5% county sales tax rate: this page describes the city only.
What ICC A117.1-2017 changes for stalls compared with the federal standard was not read; the access bullet only says the form asks for both.
The federal carpenter rate for Mobile County ($18.16, no fringe) is a 2017 survey rate, below the area's median carpenter wage on the same page.
